name: DidYouSEO — SEO Audit & Score Tracker
author: sathish27

sections.description:
DidYouSEO checks pages for 40+ technical and on-page SEO issues: titles, meta descriptions, headings, canonical tags, structured data, Open Graph tags, broken links and more. This plugin brings those scores into WordPress, so you see problems where you write.

What it adds

  • An SEO Score column in your Posts and Pages lists, colour-coded at a glance, with an “Audit now” link for anything not yet checked.
  • A block editor sidebar showing the current page’s score, with a button to re-audit it.
  • A dashboard widget with your site’s overall score and its count of critical issues and warnings.
  • Audit on publish (optional): new posts and pages are audited in the background when first published.
  • Score-drop alerts (optional): an admin notice when a page scores lower than its previous audit.

What it does not do

The plugin doesn’t change your content, your theme or your other SEO plugins’ settings. It shows scores; you decide what to fix. It works alongside Yoast SEO, Rank Math and similar plugins.

You need a DidYouSEO account

A free account at didyouseo.com is enough to start. The free plan allows 20 API requests a day; each audit and each dashboard score refresh counts as one. Paid plans raise that limit.

External services

This plugin connects to the DidYouSEO API (https://didyouseo.com/api/v1), a service run by DidYouSEO, to audit your pages and fetch scores. Nothing is sent until you connect an API key in Settings → DidYouSEO.

  • When you connect: your API key is checked, and your site’s address and name are registered with your DidYouSEO account.
  • When a page is audited (you click “Audit now” or “Audit this page”, or “Audit on publish” is on): the page’s public URL and this site’s webhook address are sent. DidYouSEO then fetches the public page, as a search engine would, and sends the result back to the webhook address. Post content is never sent from your site.
  • When the dashboard widget loads: your site’s score is requested, at most once an hour.

The service’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy apply.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from Plugins → Add New, or upload the didyouseo folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Create a free account at didyouseo.com, then create an API key under Settings → API Keys.
  4. In WordPress, go to Settings → DidYouSEO, paste the key, and click Connect.
sections.faq:
Do I need a DidYouSEO account?

Yes. A free account is enough to get started.

Does auditing use up my plan?

Each audit is one API request. The free plan allows 20 requests a day, and the dashboard widget caches its score for an hour so it doesn’t use them up.

Where is my API key stored?

In your WordPress database (the wp_options table), like other plugins’ API keys. It is never shown in the settings page after saving, and Disconnect deletes it.

How do scores get back into WordPress?

When an audit finishes, DidYouSEO sends the result to /wp-json/didyouseo/v1/webhook on your site. Each delivery is signed with a secret unique to your API key, and the plugin rejects anything without a valid signature.

Can I test on a local site?

Yes. DidYouSEO needs to reach your pages, so expose your local site with a tunnel (for example ngrok) and enter its address under Public URL (local development only).

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Its settings, stored scores and scheduled tasks are removed. Your DidYouSEO account and its data are not affected.
